original_question: For integers p, q, k with p >= q >= k >= 2, a dense-hypergraph (p,q)-theorem gives a bounded transversal number under an explicit density assumption (for example, requiring at least x n^k edges, equivalently a fixed positive edge-density level). Can this density requirement be strictly weakened, or removed entirely, while still guaranteeing a bounded transversal number from the (p,q)-property?
target_in_paper: No exact match in arXiv:0902.4207; the nearest official formulation is Section 3, Problem 2.
correct_elements: None in a paper-specific sense. The only superficial overlap is the word "transversal," but in this paper it refers to a property of the skew-symmetric matrix associated with a Volterra quadratic stochastic operator, not to a hypergraph transversal/piercing number.
missing_details: The specified paper is not about hypergraphs, the (p,q)-property, edge density, or bounded transversal numbers; it is about quadratic stochastic operators on finite-dimensional simplices.
The ambient space in the paper is the simplex S^{m-1} = {x in R^m : x_i >= 0 and sum_i x_i = 1}, and the basic object is a quadratic stochastic operator V:S^{m-1}->S^{m-1}.
A paper-faithful question must specify the heredity coefficients P_{ij,k} with P_{ij,k} >= 0, P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k}, and sum_k P_{ij,k} = 1, since these define the operator.

If the intended target is the only formal use of the term "transversal" in the paper, one must first define a Volterra QSO by the restriction P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever k is not one of i,j, and then introduce its associated skew-symmetric matrix.
In the paper, a Volterra QSO is called transversal when the associated skew-symmetric matrix has all even-order leading principal minors nonzero; this is unrelated to hypergraph hitting sets.
The draft introduces external parameters p, q, k, n, and a density threshold x n^k, but none of these notions appear in arXiv:0902.4207.
The cited arXiv paper does not contain Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; the nearest official open problem is Section 3, Problem 2.
refined_question: Let V:S^{m-1}->S^{m-1}, where S^{m-1}={x in R^m : x_i >= 0 and sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1}, be a quadratic stochastic operator given by (Vx)_k = sum_{i,j=1}^m P_{ij,k} x_i x_j, with P_{ij,k} >= 0, P_{ij,k} = P_{ji,k}, and sum_{k=1}^m P_{ij,k} = 1. A Volterra QSO is one with P_{ij,k} = 0 whenever k is not in {i,j}; in that case the associated skew-symmetric matrix is called transversal when all its even-order leading principal minors are nonzero. Can one define an analogue of transversality for an arbitrary quadratic stochastic operator, and give necessary and sufficient conditions on the heredity coefficients P under which the operator is transversal?
justification: The draft does not match the specified arXiv paper. arXiv:0902.4207 is explicitly a survey on quadratic stochastic operators: its title, abstract, introduction, and definitions all concern QSOs on simplices and their trajectories, not dense hypergraphs or (p,q)-theorems. Within this paper, the only official open problem using the term "transversal" is Section 3, Problem 2, where transversality is defined for Volterra QSOs via the associated skew-symmetric matrix. The paper also continues numbering open problems up to Problem 22, so the draft's references to "Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, Theorem 1.3" do not fit this arXiv version. Therefore the draft scores 0/10 for fidelity to arXiv:0902.4207, and the refined question above is the closest genuine paper-based target.
